hypotheses.claim: ClayCode semantic hashes containing numeric leaves require explicit type-directed numeric canonicalization rather than host-native JSON number serialization.
hypotheses.prediction: Cross-runtime host-native numeric serialization will diverge for semantically relevant edge cases while an explicit typed canonical token will remain stable on the same corpus.
hypotheses.observed: Python/Node host-native float JSON differed in 204/10000 cases; candidate typed f64 tokens differed in 0/10000; candidate exact integer tokens differed in 0/9.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production ClayCode canonicalizer can prove equivalent cross-runtime numeric semantic identity and roundtrip preservation without explicit type-directed numeric rules across the admitted numeric domain.

hypotheses.claim: Exact ClayCode Int semantics must reject or adapt lowerings to target numeric types that cannot exactly represent the source value.
hypotheses.prediction: Values outside JavaScript Number's exact integer range will change value when naively lowered to Number.
hypotheses.observed: 9007199254740993 serialized after Number conversion as 9007199254740992; 9223372036854775807 became 9223372036854776000; a 31-digit integer collapsed to 1e+30.
hypotheses.falsifier: The released target lowering either uses a proven exact integer representation for all admitted Int values or statically bounds Int so every admitted value is exactly representable on every selected backend.

hypotheses.claim: NaN, infinities and signed zero require explicit ClayCode semantic and wire policies rather than accidental host behavior.
hypotheses.prediction: Host JSON and target-runtime behavior will disagree or erase distinctions for special IEEE-754 values.
hypotheses.observed: Python emitted NaN/Infinity tokens under its default permissive JSON mode; Node JSON.stringify converted non-finite Number values to null and erased -0 in JSON presentation.
hypotheses.falsifier: The released type/effect/canonicalization contract excludes these values by type or defines and verifies a single target-independent behavior including arithmetic/replay implications.

hypotheses.claim: Raw host-native JSON number serialization is safe semantic-hash material for ClayCode numeric values.
hypotheses.counterexample: 204/10000 f64 presentation mismatches plus exact-integer loss under JS Number lowering.

hypotheses.claim: The numeric identity problem requires a new FRANK-specific ClayCode syntax or cognition primitive.
hypotheses.reason: The observed failure is resolved at typed canonical IR/checker/lowering boundaries in the bounded experiment; no executable counterexample requires FRANK-specific syntax.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production application or FRANK component demonstrates that existing typed values plus canonicalizer/lowering contracts cannot express the required numeric semantics.
